state: TeleDoc context: a Go Telegram bot ingests documents posted to a channel (long polling, handlers deliberately serialized because the SQLite store is single-writer). For every ingested document the bot sets an emoji reaction on that message; the channel's reactions double as the archive's status indicator (archived / duplicate / tagging-failed-needs-attention). Incident: a user mass-resends ~80 files to backfill the archive; ingestion succeeds for each (log shows 'archived ...' lines about 1 second apart), but setting each reaction hits Telegram's flood control: 'too many requests: retry after 38... 37... 36... 31... 29' — the per-chat reaction quota is exhausted, each subsequent call returns HTTP 429 with a decreasing retry_after, and every reaction is currently lost (they are only logged and swallowed). The bot library (go-telegram/bot) returns errors as *TooManyRequestsError{RetryAfter int} and has NO built-in rate limiter or retry. Constraints: (1) ingestion of subsequent documents must not stall for tens of seconds — during a mass import the serialized handler would otherwise stop archiving while a reaction sleeps; (2) the reactions matter: the tagging-failed reaction (🤔) is how the user learns a document needs attention, so silently dropping reactions is only acceptable as a last resort; (3) the fix should also stop the wall of 429 log lines; (4) the same flood control can hit the one-shot getFile call the web UI makes when a user clicks download, though there the request must fail reasonably fast rather than hang the browser.

reaction_flood_strategy.instructions: How should the bot handle reaction calls that hit Telegram flood control (429 + retry_after)?

criteria.async_queue_worker: Reactions go through a per-process background queue: the ingestion path only enqueues (never blocks), one worker goroutine sends them paced ~1/second, and on 429 it waits retry_after (plus a small buffer) and retries that reaction a bounded number of times before giving up with one clear log line.
criteria.inline_blocking_retry: Keep reactions synchronous in the ingestion path but sleep retry_after and retry a bounded number of times — simple, but a 30-40s sleep stalls archiving of every subsequent document during a mass import.
criteria.drop_on_flood: Accept the loss: on 429 just log once and move on — zero complexity, but mass imports lose all status reactions including the tagging-failed warning.

proactive_pacing.instructions: Besides retrying after a 429, should the bot pace reaction calls proactively?

criteria.pace_one_per_second: Yes: the worker always waits ~1s between reaction calls (well under Telegram's observed per-chat reaction quota, and the incident's retry_after countdown of 38→29s over ~9s implies the bucket refills about 1/second).
criteria.reactive_only: No pacing: send immediately and rely purely on 429 retry_after backoff.

async_ingestion_ok.instructions: Is it acceptable that with the queue approach a document's reaction may appear on the message several seconds (or during heavy floods, minutes) after the 'archived' log line, since ingestion no longer waits for the reaction?

criteria.true: Acceptable: the reaction is a status indicator, not a transactional guarantee; eventual arrival is fine.
criteria.false: Not acceptable: the reaction must be set before the document counts as processed.

retry_budget.instructions: How many times should the worker retry one reaction before giving up (each 429 supplies a fresh retry_after, so a retry loop could in principle chase the quota forever)?

criteria.three_attempts: 3 attempts total: survive a burst, but give up within ~1-2 minutes worst case.
criteria.five_attempts: 5 attempts total: longer persistence, up to ~4-5 minutes worst case.
criteria.until_success: Keep retrying indefinitely while the process lives — guarantees every reaction eventually lands but a permanently flooded chat means unbounded queue growth.

getfile_retry.instructions: Should the web UI's one-shot getFile call (user clicked download; browser is waiting) also retry on 429, but with a small total wait budget (~10 seconds) after which it fails with a clear error?

criteria.true: Yes: retry within a ~10s budget, then fail with the flood error message.
criteria.false: No: one attempt only, fail immediately on 429.
